Synopsis

mistralai 2.4.6 carried a Linux-only import hook in mistralai/client/__init__.py. It downloaded transformers.pyz from attacker infrastructure and ran it detached.

Story

The PyPI side of Shai-Hulud used a different shape from the npm worm. Instead of a `preinstall` script, `mistralai@2.4.6` placed its loader in `mistralai/client/__init__.py`, where ordinary imports could trigger it.

The loader was Linux-only and guarded itself with `MISTRAL_INIT` to avoid repeated execution. It downloaded `transformers.pyz` from `83.142.209.194` using `curl -k -L -s`, wrote it under `/tmp`, and launched it with the current Python interpreter.

JFrog later reported that the remote PyPI payload had changed from attribution text to a credential stealer. The observed target set included local files, cloud provider credentials, Kubernetes, Vault, password managers, and developer tooling secrets.

This record is scoped to Mistral's Python SDK artifact. The broader campaign record carries the cross-ecosystem TeamPCP/Shai-Hulud machinery and propagation behavior.
